articles.summary: Multiple system outages have hit the US in November, causing disruptions to essential services such as air travel, online banking, and classified national security communications.
articles.content: Multiple system outages have hit the US in November, causing disruptions to essential services. A significant outage on November 12 affected Microsoft's Outlook email service, leaving users without access to their emails for several hours. In recent days, a Delta system outage has caused travel chaos, with passengers stranded due to technical issues. The month of November has seen a wave of disruptions across the US, including a nationwide ground stop of all air travel and an outage affecting classified national security communications. A disruption to online banking services has also been reported, leaving customers unable to access their accounts. As governments around the world advise households to prepare for potential emergencies, anxiety and conspiracy theories are spreading online. In today's world, where technology reigns supreme, it's essential to be prepared for everyday disruptions. According to experts, households should not view emergency preparedness as a one-time task but rather an ongoing process that requires continuous practice. To start, let's consider the common short-term outages we experience with internet, cell service, and website connectivity. While these events can be frustrating, they often resolve themselves quickly, either by waiting it out or resetting our home router. However, if you're unsure whether the issue is widespread or isolated to your area, there are resources available. Downdetector is a useful tool for checking if others in your region are experiencing similar connectivity issues. By visiting the site, you can see the number of people who've reported an outage and view the most recent and severe incidents at the top of their homepage. This information can help determine whether the problem lies with your provider or is a more widespread issue. In situations where cell service outages occur, having a backup plan in place can be beneficial. This could involve using a different mobile device, like a phone or tablet, or an internet hotspot that operates on a separate network from your primary service provider. Having cash on hand is essential in case of an extended internet outage that disrupts payment systems. This may seem old-fashioned in today's digital age, but it's a prudent measure to take. A modest amount will suffice, and there's no need to hoard gold bars. Experts emphasize the importance of having a backup plan that functions even when technology fails. As one expert noted, "The whole idea is to have a plan that works when technologies fail." This mindset is crucial in preparing for potential disruptions. While November's outages did not include widespread electricity blackouts, experts have warned about the possibility of such events occurring in the future. Even nationwide blackouts are not ruled out, which could lead to significant disruptions. Preparing for an outage involves having essential supplies readily available at home. According to guidelines from Ready.gov, this includes keeping water, flashlights, batteries, food, and a first aid kit on hand. Portable chargers should also be easily accessible to charge devices like cell phones. In addition to these basic supplies, individuals can take extra precautions by investing in backup power sources for sensitive data devices. A UPS (uninterruptible power supply) is crucial for protecting computers and backup drives from power outages. A lack of power could have serious consequences for families relying on medical equipment at home. When it comes to medical needs, a specific backup plan should be discussed with healthcare providers to ensure continuity of care, according to experts. Powering medical equipment with portable generators is not advisable, as carbon monoxide poisoning can occur due to improper use in enclosed spaces. The risk of carbon monoxide poisoning is particularly high when using gas-powered portable generators indoors or in confined areas. This highlights the importance of having a reliable plan in place for emergency situations. When preparing for everyday disruptions, it's essential to have a reliable plan in place that considers the needs of all family members. This includes setting up a meeting spot where everyone can reconnect if they get separated during an emergency. A predetermined meeting point can help avoid confusion and anxiety when phone lines are down or communication is disrupted. As Reynolds emphasizes, "it is not hoarding or stockpiling" to have enough supplies on hand to sustain your family for a short period of time. articles.title: Galaxy Z Fold 8 Review: A Customizable Phone with Limitations
articles.summary: The Galaxy Z Fold 8 offers a highly customizable software experience and sleek design, but has limitations in its cover screen customization options.
articles.content: The latest phone to capture my attention is the Galaxy Z Fold 8, a foldable device that has managed to maintain its appeal even after several months on the market. A key factor in this phone's enduring charm is its sleek and symmetrical design, which feels surprisingly thin and lightweight despite its large size. However, it's not just aesthetics that set the Galaxy Z Fold 8 apart - its software experience is also highly customizable, allowing users to tailor their settings to suit their preferences. Out of the box, the phone's software can feel a bit restrictive, with a locked home screen layout on the cover display and camera settings that don't quite live up to their potential. Fortunately, these limitations can be easily overcome by diving into additional tools beyond the standard Settings menu - but only after investing some time in setting up the device. The process of getting the most out of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 involves installing a few apps, tweaking various settings and adding new plugins through Samsung's Good Lock app. The Galaxy Z Fold 8's cover screen has limitations when it comes to customization. Specifically, users are restricted to a four-column layout on their home screen, even if they reduce the icon size. This can result in wasted space and an inefficient use of the available real estate. To make better use of this space, consider downloading the Home Up plugin through Samsung's Good Lock app. Located under the Plugins tab, it allows users to change the layout and place icons anywhere on the home screen. With this feature, users can arrange up to seven apps in a row or column for a 7-by-7 layout. One of the benefits of installing the Home Up plugin is improved organization and aesthetics. By placing frequently used apps and folders on one side of the home screen, users can access them quickly with minimal hand movement. This can be particularly useful when using the device in one-hand mode. System UI elements located on the left side or top of the screen can also pose a challenge for ergonomic use. For instance, accessing the Quick Settings Panel requires a swipe down from the top, which can necessitate readjusting one's grip. To mitigate this issue, users may want to consider installing One Hand Operation Plus. This additional plugin allows users to reassign system UI elements to more accessible locations on the screen. By doing so, they can minimize the need for hand adjustments and maintain a comfortable grip on the device. This feature is particularly useful for those who prioritize one-hand use. The combination of Home Up and One Hand Operation Plus plugins can significantly enhance the user experience on the Galaxy Z Fold 8. By optimizing layout and reassigning system UI elements, users can make better use of the available space and enjoy a more seamless interaction with their device. With Good Lock plugins, users have more control over their Galaxy Z Fold 8's layout and functionality. One such plugin is the ability to add gesture handles to both sides of the screen, allowing for customizable interactions. The left and right side gestures can be programmed to perform various tasks, including reassigning Android's default swipe back gesture. This added flexibility enables users to personalize their device according to their preferences. One Hand Operation Plus offers even more customization options by letting users add up to six shortcuts within the Short swipe and Long swipe gestures. Straight, Diagonal up, and Diagonal down swipes are among the choices available for these shortcuts. Customizing these gestures can greatly enhance daily usage of the Galaxy Z Fold 8. For instance, setting a diagonal swipe down from the right side to access Quick Settings can be a convenient change over time. In addition to gesture customization, users can also fine-tune their device's touch area by adjusting the Width, Size, and Position within One Hand Operation Plus settings. This allows for more precise control when interacting with the screen. The Galaxy Z Fold 8's camera capabilities have limitations compared to its siblings, such as the lack of a telephoto lens for optical zoom. However, users can still improve digital zoom results by adjusting settings within the Camera app. When using the Galaxy Z Fold 8's camera features, many users overlook a crucial tool that can significantly enhance their photography experience: the Samsung Camera Assistant app. To access these hidden settings, navigate to the Camera app on your device and tap the four-dot menu in the top right corner. This will open up a range of options, including Settings > Camera Assistant > Install. Installing this app is highly recommended for anyone looking to get the most out of their Galaxy Z Fold 8's camera capabilities. One of the first settings you should adjust is the resolution. While the default setting is 12 megapixels, it's worth changing this to 24 megapixels for more detailed shots and better results at both 2x and 4x zoom levels. This can be done by going into the Camera settings and making the necessary adjustments. When you're in the Camera Assistant app, take a moment to enable the 2x crop zoom shortcut. This simple tweak will allow you to access 2x zoom more quickly from within the viewfinder, streamlining your photography workflow. By setting the default resolution to 24 megapixels, users can achieve sharper photos with improved clarity at both 1x and 0.6x zoom levels without sacrificing too much storage space. For optimal results at 4x zoom, consider switching to a 50-megapixel resolution for images that rival those posted on Instagram. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 offers a revamped multitasking experience that maximizes its dual screens. By default, the device splits the screen into a 90:10 ratio, allowing users to have one application take up most of the space while still having another app visible. This configuration is particularly useful when working on documents and needing quick access to reference materials. The user can type away in a Google Doc without interruption, with their research material conveniently displayed alongside. Dragging and dropping apps within this multitasking mode has also become more intuitive. Users must first navigate to the Recents menu by swiping up and holding on the home screen, before tapping and holding an app to relocate it to either half of the screen or use as a pop-up application. The Recents menu retains user-defined app groupings for easy access, making it effortless to switch between multiple applications. articles.content: A vintage coat can instantly elevate any outfit and become an enduring expression of personal style. This is a fact I've come to appreciate through my exploration of fashion and self-expression. In many cases, a well-crafted vintage coat has the power to transport and transform its wearer. While searching for unique pieces that reflect my personality, I've found it increasingly difficult to find modern coats with the same level of detail and character as those from past eras. There's something about a vintage coat that's hard to replicate today - perhaps it's the intricate craftsmanship or the ability to tell a story through its very fabric. My latest discovery is an antique raspberry silk velvet mini cape adorned with ruched ruffles and a large, ornate clasp. Its understated label belies its exceptional beauty and uniqueness, making it a true standout in my collection. When it comes to expressing one's personal style through clothing, there's a fine line between making a statement and being overwhelmed by the garment itself. A vintage coat can strike the perfect balance, offering a unique conversation starter that doesn't overshadow its wearer. In my own collection, some of the most striking pieces have been acquired by chance, rather than deliberate search. These coats serve as versatile building blocks for outfits, allowing me to create a wide range of looks with ease. Whether I'm looking to make a bold statement or keep things understated, they're always up to the task. The thrill of hunting down the perfect vintage coat lies in its unpredictability, and that's exactly what makes it so appealing. By disregarding traditional rules and shopping purely on instinct, I've developed a keen eye for spotting truly exceptional pieces. Color, texture, length, and silhouette are my guiding principles, often leading me to dramatic, extraordinary, or even slightly strange designs that add an extra layer of personality to any outfit. The thrill of the hunt for unique and extraordinary pieces has led to some incredible discoveries, like the Pucci coat that was an unexpected find online. A reverse image search quest led to the unearthing of a cropped Chantal Thomass feather jacket, its textural beauty so captivating that it became an instant must-have. The 1960s rainbow quilted coat, on the other hand, found me in a warehouse sale, its vibrant colors and intricate quilting creating a striking contrast against a modern backdrop. Vintage coats possess qualities that are impossible to replicate, making each piece truly one-of-a-kind. They aren't trying to be something they're not; their unique personality is what makes them so special. The right vintage coat can elevate personal style in a way that's hard to achieve with newer pieces. It's proof that history and individuality go hand-in-hand when it comes to fashion. In the end, collecting vintage coats is about embracing imperfection and celebrating the quirks that make each piece truly unforgettable. articles.title: Azerbaijani Opposition Leader Ali Karimli Spends Year Behind Bars Awaiting Trial on Charges of Attempting to Seize Power by Force
articles.summary: Ali Karimli, chairman of the Azerbaijani Popular Front Party (APFP), has been detained alongside his political adviser Mammad Ibrahim since November last year.
articles.content: Azerbaijani opposition leader Ali Karimli has spent a year behind bars, awaiting trial on charges of attempting to seize power by force. Karimli, chairman of the Azerbaijani Popular Front Party (APFP), denies the allegations, calling them politically motivated and an attempt to silence him. His party is one of Azerbaijan's main opposition parties, and he has been a vocal critic of the government. Alongside Karimli is his longtime political adviser and senior party official Mammad Ibrahim, who is no stranger to prison life. In 2016, Ibrahim was sentenced to three years on hooliganism charges that Human Rights Watch criticized as baseless. He was detained again in November last year, this time alongside Karimli. The State Security Service has charged both men under Article 278.1 of the Criminal Code, which carries a possible prison sentence of 12 to 20 years, or life imprisonment, for actions aimed at forcibly seizing power or changing Azerbaijan's constitutional order. The allegations against Karimli suggest that he planned to capitalize on a large rally in Baku last July to spark unrest and gain control of key government institutions. However, according to Karimli himself, his party was not involved in organizing the event, and he did not even attend it. Karimli's lawyer has maintained that both defendants believe their prosecution is politically motivated, and this view is shared by human rights groups. Shortly after the arrest, Amnesty International called for Karimli's release unless concrete evidence of a crime could be produced. Amnesty's deputy director for Eastern Europe and Central Asia, Denis Krivosheev, stated that Karimli's detention represents another example of Azerbaijan's slide into authoritarianism. He also noted that the government appears to have no qualms about suppressing all forms of dissent in the country. The court motion submitted on November 3 highlights Karimli's desire for change in Azerbaijan, but he has consistently rejected the use of violence as a means to achieve this goal. Karimli has maintained that he will only accept power through democratic elections, a stance he reiterated in writing. However, his call for charges against him to be dropped was met with rejection by the court. The opposition leader also disputed the prosecution's claims about the National Council of Democratic Forces, an opposition coalition established in 2013. He argued that the group's formation was transparent and aimed at supporting a joint opposition candidate in the presidential election, rather than plotting a coup. Karimli has denied any collaboration with Mehdiyev, the former head of the presidential administration, stating they have never met or communicated despite decades of opposing political views. Mehdiyev's lawyer corroborated Karimli's claim, asserting that his client also denies any connection to him. The trial against Karimli and Ibrahim is being held behind closed doors, with foreign diplomats barred from entry. Lawyer Nazim Musayev justified the secrecy by citing state secrets as a reason for the proceedings' closure. The family of opposition leader Ali Karimli has been struggling to maintain contact with him since his detention a year ago. Turkel Karimli's last conversation with his father took place in late April or early May, and since then, both he and their mother have had their phone calls and face-to-face visits denied. According to information received by the family from lawyers, the authorities had temporarily halted food parcel deliveries over the summer. The amount of additional drinking water allowed was severely restricted, with only 5 liters available per week. This meager allowance reportedly led to severe dehydration during an August 6 court hearing, where Karimli fainted. The situation has slightly improved since then, with food deliveries permitted again and a promise made to increase the weekly water allowance from 5 to 10 liters. However, the family's concerns about Karimli's well-being persist, as his weight has significantly decreased during his time in prison. Karimli has also complained of persistent noise disrupting his sleep, restricted family contact, worsening back pain, and poor ventilation in his cell. Rights groups have expressed concern over these conditions, warning that they could amount to torture or other ill treatment due to the lack of access to clean drinking water and proper ventilation. The family of detained opposition leader has expressed concerns about his medical treatment in custody, citing kidney problems and insomnia. Several examinations by doctors appointed by the authorities have been conducted on the detainee, but the family has also sought outside medical expertise to ensure he receives proper care. Family visits are a rare privilege for the detainee, with communication often hindered by the facility's rules. His wife is permitted to see him through a glass partition twice a month and deliver food and supplies once a week. The detainee's imprisonment has had far-reaching consequences, not only for his family but also for the party he leads. The international community's criticism of Azerbaijan's handling of opposition leader Ali Karimli's detention continues to grow. European lawmakers have condemned his imprisonment, calling for his immediate release along with other political prisoners in the country. They also urged Azerbaijani authorities to ensure that those behind bars receive proper medical care and access to legal representation. The European Parliament adopted a resolution on October 8, emphasizing the need for Karimli's unconditional freedom. The lawmakers' move was seen as a significant step in highlighting Azerbaijan's human rights record. Meanwhile, Karimli himself received recognition for his work when he was awarded the 2026 Magnitsky Human Rights Award earlier this month. Azerbaijani Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov faced questions about Karimli's arrest at a joint press conference with his German counterpart on November 18 in Baku. When asked about the opposition leader's detention, Bayramov maintained that those who belong to the opposition are not exempt from facing legal consequences. He stated that the case would be handled according to Azerbaijani law and left it up to the court to make a final decision. articles.title: Arsenal's Goal-Scoring Rate Remains a Concern This Season
articles.summary: Despite having some talented players, Arsenal's goal-scoring rate is lower than last year's, with 30 goals in 18 games across all competitions.
articles.content: Arsenal's attack has been a topic of discussion among fans and experts alike, with Mikel Arteta repeatedly expressing his desire for his team to score more goals. Despite having some talented players on their roster, Arsenal's goal-scoring rate this season is lower than last year's, when every goal was hard-won. The Gunners have 30 goals in 18 games across all competitions, a far cry from the 114 goals they scored in the previous campaign. Arteta would argue that variance could be the reason behind their lackluster performance so far this season. However, numbers tell a different story, suggesting that there may be more to it than just bad luck. In an interview, Arteta pointed out that his team has improved in various areas except for goal-scoring. He mentioned that they had a similar period of poor form last season and even questioned the role of luck in their current predicament. Luck indeed seems to play a significant part in determining the outcome of some games. Take Tuesday's Champions League draw against Borussia Dortmund, where Serhou Guirassy hit the post twice, only to see the ball bounce out instead of going in. Arteta is confident that his team will turn things around and start scoring more goals soon. He expressed full trust in his players and their abilities to perform well every three days. However, it remains to be seen whether Arteta's words will translate into action on the pitch. The numbers do suggest some improvement in certain areas, such as shots per game and expected goals. To determine if Arsenal has truly improved across all competitions, one needs to consider data from multiple seasons. Doing so reveals that the team is on an upward trend in several key statistics. The comparison between an all-competitions data set for 2026-27 and completed seasons reveals a potential issue when evaluating Arsenal's performance. The extra non-Premier League games played by the team are often against lower-standard opposition, which may skew the numbers. To get a more accurate picture, it might be best to focus solely on Premier League matches. When doing so, the data shows a different trend. There have been periods in the past where Arsenal's attacking prowess was lacking, but overall, their 2026-27 season is not as strong as previous years under Mikel Arteta. One key statistic that stands out is the number of shots taken by Arsenal per game, which has decreased to 13.7 this season. This is one fewer shot than last season and marks a new low for the team in any Premier League season under Arteta since 2020-21. The expected goals (xG) per game have also dropped from 1.71 to 1.6. The goal tally for Arsenal has followed a similar trend, with the team on pace to score fewer goals than last season. This is surprising given that they won the title scoring so few goals in previous years. Their defense has been strong, but it's hard to believe they can win another title with such a low-scoring attack. The contrast between Arsenal's current form and their past success is striking. Statistically, their attack appears to be holding them back this season. However, it's worth noting that the team looks more entertaining to watch than last year's squad. Despite this, there are still some worrying signs for Arsenal fans. The team has struggled against stronger opponents, with matches like the one at Nottingham Forest showcasing their difficulties in breaking down well-organized defenses. This is a common problem faced by many teams in the Premier League. The depth of athletic talent in the English top flight means that even well-drilled teams can be difficult to break down. However, this also highlights the importance of having a strong attacking unit. For Arsenal, their lack of goals and shots on goal is a major concern as they look to defend their title. In conclusion, Arsenal's attack looks like it could be a limiting factor for their prospects this season. Despite some encouraging signs, the team's numbers suggest that they are not as strong as they were last year. The team's fortunes seem to be shifting in their favor, despite some lingering issues. Key factors that hindered them last season have eased this year, giving them a renewed sense of purpose. The weight of not being champions has been lifted, freeing them from the pressure that came with it. As a result, they're able to focus on the game at hand. The team's injury woes are also behind them, which is allowing players like Martin Odegaard to regain their form. His creative spark was noticeably absent last season due to injuries, but he's back to his old self now. This has had a positive impact on the team's overall performance, particularly in the attacking department. One player who's stepped up this season is Noni Madueke. He's been leading the Premier League in combined shots and chances created per 90 minutes, which is no small feat. His contributions have been invaluable to the team, and he's shown himself to be a reliable option for Arteta. The absence of Bukayo Saka has not held them back as much as expected. They've managed to compensate for his loss with other players, such as Kai Havertz, who's fit again after a spell on the sidelines. Viktor Gyokeres has also improved significantly, providing another creative outlet for the team. Bruno Guimaraes' defensive vulnerabilities are being somewhat offset by his exceptional passing range. He's able to pick out teammates with precision, which is allowing them to exploit weaknesses in the opposition's defense. However, it's worth noting that his defensive flaws still exist, and Arteta will need to find a way to mitigate those. Recent games have shown that Arsenal are capable of producing high-quality performances when they're at their best. They laid down 30 shots on Bundesliga leaders Dortmund, which is an impressive feat. It remains to be seen whether this level of performance can be sustained over the course of a full season. Arteta has always been keen to experiment with different formations and lineups. This season, he's taken it to new heights by introducing players who can operate in multiple positions. Jurrien Timber and Piero Hincapie have become particularly adept at adapting their roles, which is allowing them to exploit weaknesses in the opposition. The introduction of Christos Tzolis has given Arteta a new option on the left flank. He's been allowed to roam freely from one side of the pitch to the other, which has caused problems for opposing teams' defenses. This level of flexibility is something that not many teams possess, and it's giving Arsenal an edge over their competitors. Arteta's emphasis on positional versatility has paid dividends in recent games. The team's ability to adapt to different situations has allowed them to stay one step ahead of the opposition. However, despite these encouraging signs, the team's numbers suggest that they are not as strong as they were last year. Arsenal's attacking woes continue to be a concern for manager Mikel Arteta despite an improvement in their open-play performance. Arteta is adjusting tactics to suit his team's strengths and weaknesses, acknowledging that they have made significant progress in understanding what it takes to score goals. The evidence suggests that Arsenal are indeed more threatening on the pitch than previously, with impressive numbers from open play in all competitions. Their xG from open play has surpassed any season since 2023-24, when they scored an astonishing 91 Premier League goals. Meanwhile, they have achieved double figures for open-play shots, a feat they only managed during their early years of title contention. However, the team's inability to convert these chances into actual goals remains a puzzle that needs solving. Arteta's preference is clear: he wants his team to win comfortably, not just by a single goal margin. The pressure on Arsenal to score more goals increases with each match, particularly against top-tier opponents who can capitalize on any moment of weakness. Arsenal's manager has addressed concerns that his team is too comfortable when leading by a goal, but the data suggests otherwise. The xG totals for Arsenal at home have been surprisingly low this season, and it seems that their tendency to lead games might be contributing to this issue. When they are ahead, their attack becomes below-average, averaging just 1.22 xG per 90 minutes. This trend is not new; fans of the team will recognize that Arsenal often rely on defending well and grinding out tight wins rather than creating scoring opportunities. Their past success in these situations may be playing on their minds, making them more cautious in attack. Manager Mikel Arteta acknowledged this possibility when questioned about his team's approach to games where they are leading by a goal. He pointed out that the opposition can often capitalize on any moment of weakness if Arsenal fail to finish off the game. The numbers suggest that Arsenal have been particularly effective at managing these types of situations over the past few years, but it is unclear whether this will continue as the team faces increasingly strong opponents. One reason for Arsenal's struggles in attack may be their reliance on set pieces. While they were once a key source of goals, their output has decreased significantly this season. They are creating fewer chances from dead-ball situations and converting even fewer. The data shows that Arsenal are taking fewer corners than in previous seasons, with an average of 5.4 per game - their lowest figure in six years. In contrast to last season's numbers, they are not generating as many scoring opportunities from these set pieces. This decrease in corners is not unique to Arsenal; the league-wide trend suggests that teams are giving up fewer corners across the board. However, it is likely that Arsenal's own defensive solidity is contributing to this trend. Opponents have also become more cautious when facing Arsenal, taking fewer risks and opting for a more defensive approach. This has led to a decrease in scoring opportunities for both teams. The numbers suggest that Arsenal are struggling to create goals from their set pieces, with an average of 1.3 shots resulting from these situations. In contrast, last season's figure was significantly higher at 2.0 shots per game. Arsenal's attack has undergone a significant transformation, with a notable decrease in shots per game this season compared to last year. The team's reliance on set pieces has diminished, as they now focus on controlling possession and dominating the attacking third of the field. This shift in strategy is yielding more touches and time for players to create scoring opportunities, but so far, the goals have been elusive. With a strong defensive record, Arsenal can afford to be patient and await the breakthrough that will restore their attack to its former glory. articles.title: Veracruz's Hidden Riches Revealed Through Culinary Exploration
articles.summary: A senior chef and food expert has been exploring the often-overlooked state of Veracruz in eastern Mexico, discovering its rich cultural heritage and unspoiled natural beauty.
articles.content: A senior chef and food expert has been exploring the often-overlooked state of Veracruz in eastern Mexico, discovering its rich cultural heritage and unspoiled natural beauty. The archaeological site at El Tajín was our first stop on this culinary journey, where we witnessed a bustling entrance filled with vendors selling colorful embroidered dresses and intricately glazed ceramics. However, as we passed through the gates, the crowds dissipated, revealing a tranquil atmosphere that allowed us to fully appreciate the impressive pre-Columbian pyramids. Lucho Martínez, chef and founder of Mexico City's Michelin-starred restaurant Em, accompanied me on this trip and shared his unique perspective on Veracruz. When I visit during the week, he said, "it's completely empty. As we walked through the site, he pointed out the magnificent six-terraced structure with 365 carved niches set against a lush hillside backdrop. The Totonac people are believed to have built this remarkable structure, which seems almost forgotten in its stillness. Martínez glanced around at the peaceful surroundings and said, It feels left to itself. This sentiment echoed our own experience of Veracruz as we ventured further into the state, finding a mix of rugged coastline, dense jungle, and vibrant cultural heritage that seemed waiting to be explored. Veracruz boasts an incredible natural landscape, featuring towering green mountains that give way to long stretches of dark volcanic gray-sand beaches. The rugged coastline is a sight to behold, with its dramatic cliffs and secluded coves waiting to be explored. Despite the state's many charms, it remains relatively off the beaten path for tourists. Many visitors flock to more popular destinations like Riviera Maya and Cabo San Lucas, which offer a more established tourist infrastructure. However, these areas can't compare to the authentic experience that Veracruz has to offer. Chef Lucho Martínez is one of the few who regularly visit his home state in search of fresh ingredients and a respite from the fast-paced life of Mexico City. Born in Coatzacoalcos, he left for the US at age 5 with his mother before returning to Veracruz at 14. Martínez's culinary career took off after he moved to Cancún and later to Mexico City, where he opened his first restaurant, Emilia, named after his daughter. The restaurant relocated in 2020 and was rechristened Em, earning one of the coveted Michelin stars for its innovative Mexican cuisine. As we set out on our journey to Veracruz, Chef Lucho Martínez emphasized the region's often-overlooked produce, citing vanilla and coffee as prime examples of its rich bounty. Our destination was Mexico City, where Martínez had a coffee stand called Café Tormenta serving brews made from beans sourced from Veracruz. This was our starting point before embarking on a weekend trip to explore the places he holds dear in the state. Martínez sources 90 percent of his ingredients from Veracruz, including vanilla, which is a key component of his innovative Mexican cuisine at Em, earning one of the coveted Michelin stars. We planned to drive four hours north-northwest out of Mexico City to San Rafael, a small town settled by French immigrants in the 19th century. Martínez was restoring a house there and wanted us to see it. The winding road took us through colossal green mountains as we cruised along a narrow two-lane highway, eventually pulling into Gaya, where we visited a vanilla farm run by the same family since 1873 when they arrived from Italy. As we continued our journey through Veracruz, we made our way to Gutiérrez Zamora, a charming town nestled along the banks of the Tecolutla River. The main drag was lined with bustling storefronts, and Chef Lucho Martínez expertly navigated us to La Galera, an open-air café that caught his eye. La Galera's menu offered a mouth-watering array of local specialties, including cheese empanadas, molotes, and gorditas. Our simple wood table was soon filled with steaming plates of these delicious dishes, accompanied by the gentle whirring of fans above us as they sliced through the humid air. Martínez couldn't resist drizzling cream over a warm, puffed-up gordita, proclaiming it an all-day breakfast" that's all about customization. He's so enamored with this traditional dish that he's even replaced a bread course in one of his recipes with a crispy gordita, topped with crème fraîche and the indulgent touch of caviar. As we finished our meal and hit the road once more, we found ourselves surrounded by banana plantations and lemon groves, their lush foliage whacking against the car's roof. We were now in the outskirts of San Rafael, a picturesque area dotted with buildings in a distinctive French Provincial style that added to its charm. We made a brief stop to admire Chef Martínez's home, a long, low-slung structure with wood-shuttered windows and a pitched roof adorned with little scalloped tiles. A wide veranda, supported by elegant white columns, provided the perfect spot to take in the serene surroundings of this tranquil neighborhood. The nearby hotel to Martínez's home is Maison Couturier, a charming design-focused establishment that originated from a 19th-century agricultural estate. Located in town, it was converted by Grupo Habita, a hospitality brand based in Mexico City. Unfortunately, the hotel was fully booked during our stay. We had no choice but to head to its sister property on the Costa Esmeralda beach, a 30-minute drive away along a scenic highway that runs parallel to the sea. The stretch of road is dotted with storied sun-bleached resorts, each one nestled between the highway and the sand. One such resort is Hotel Azúcar, our base for the night. This cluster of whitewashed buildings tumbles onto the beach, providing an idyllic setting for a seaside stay. We spent some time on the shore, with our feet deep in the charcoal-hued sand, watching families splash in the warm and shallow water. The atmosphere was tranquil, with no sign of tourists flocking to this part of Mexico. We grabbed a table at the hotel restaurant, located just a few steps from the sea, and enjoyed the gentle breeze as the sun began to set. We ordered plates of freshly grilled seafood, cooked by a woman standing over an open flame. The meal was simple yet satisfying, with no pretentious menu or elaborate wine list to speak of. The warm morning sun broke over San Rafael as we made our way back to Maison Couturier for breakfast. The lush grounds beckoned us to take a stroll before settling in at an old farmhouse table, where Chef Lucho Martínez was already seated. He ordered his favorite dish: esponjaditas with crème fraîche and eggs in a rich tomato sauce, a simple yet satisfying meal that contrasted nicely with the previous evening's elaborate feast. The flavors were a testament to Veracruz's culinary prowess, even if the menu lacked pretension. The drive back to Mexico City was long but fueled by a stop at Nakú Restaurante Papanteco in Tajín, where traditional dancers and women pressing tortillas on a comal created a lively atmosphere that drew us in. articles.title: Spain Holds General Election Amid Housing Crisis Protests
articles.summary: The election has significant implications for Europe as it will determine who takes Spain's prime minister's place at the negotiating table.
articles.content: Spain is holding a general election that has far-reaching implications for Europe, as one of its most influential leaders prepares to leave office. Pedro Sanchez, Spain's prime minister and leader of the center-left Socialists, has been a prominent voice in European politics for over eight years. His country is not only the largest EU member state still governed by a social democratic government but also one of the few remaining. This election will determine who takes his place at the negotiating table. The election was triggered after parliament rejected two emergency decrees aimed at addressing Spain's housing crisis, which has been a major source of discontent for Spaniards this year. Sanchez called the snap election just three days later, amid widespread protests against rising housing costs nationwide. Polls suggest a closely contested race between the conservative People's Party and the Socialists, with both parties neck-and-neck according to recent predictions. The outcome of Spain's election has significant implications for Europe's center left, as a change in government would silence one of its most influential voices on the continent. Javier Carbonell, a policy analyst at the European Policy Centre in Brussels, warns that this voice could be silenced if the right-wing populist Vox party gains power. Carbonell highlights three key positions that have set Sanchez apart from other EU leaders: his willingness to challenge US President Donald Trump's policies, his support for Palestinian statehood, and his defense of immigration into Europe. These stances have earned him a reputation as a champion of progressive values in the region. Sanchez has been one of the few EU leaders who continue to argue that migrant workers are essential to filling labor shortages, supporting an aging population, and driving economic growth. His government's decision to grant legal status to eligible migrants already living in Spain is seen as a key factor in this year's economic expansion. The success of Sanchez's policies can be measured by the fact that his government opened a program to grant legal status to eligible migrants earlier this year, which received over 1 million applications. This move has contributed to Spain's robust economy, with GDP growing by 2.6% last year and expected to continue growing at a similar rate in the coming years. The ongoing election campaign could still be influenced by recent events, including the train disaster that occurred earlier this year, which may have impacted Sanchez's chances of winning re-election. The conservative PP has campaigned for stricter immigration controls while preserving pathways for foreign workers in industries facing labor shortages. This stance is not unique to Spain, as it aligns with a broader trend across Europe where governments are pushing for tougher immigration policies. A closer look at the continent reveals that several countries are already exploring ways to strengthen return policies and deter asylum seekers whose claims have been rejected. Countries such as Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece, and the Netherlands are engaged in discussions with Rwanda about establishing a hub for individuals whose asylum applications have been denied. This development is part of a larger effort to streamline repatriation processes. Experts like Camino Mortera-Martinez at the Centre for European Reform emphasize that this shift towards stricter immigration policies is driven by voter sentiment rather than leadership initiatives. Spain's defense policies could undergo a significant transformation if the country changes government in the upcoming election. This shift may have far-reaching implications for its European neighbors, particularly as it relates to NATO's defense spending targets. Sanchez has been critical of NATO's new annual target of 5% of GDP by 2035, which includes both military expenditure and broader security investments. He believes that Spain can meet its NATO capability commitments by allocating around 2.1% of GDP for defense purposes. This stance diverges from the alliance's stated goal. Both the PP and Vox parties favor higher defense investment but have left the exact figure open in their election programs. It appears that a significant portion of their voting base supports increased defense spending, unlike Sanchez who has expressed reservations about NATO's new target. A change in Spain's approach to the Middle East is also anticipated if Sanchez loses the election. The country's current government has been at the forefront of defending international law and human rights, particularly in its dealings with Israel. A new conservative government in Spain would likely result in reduced vocal support for the Palestinian cause, according to analysts. Sanchez's influence on the issue has been significant, moving the consensus towards a more pro-Palestine stance. The loss of Sanchez in Sunday's election could have far-reaching implications for Europe's social democrats, potentially weakening their grip as the strongest center-left force among EU member states. The defeat may also spark a wider debate within the European center left about how to regain voter support and maintain political relevance across the continent. articles.title: New Adaptation of Pride and Prejudice Underway
articles.summary: Screenwriter Dolly Alderton shares her behind-the-scenes look at making the television event of the year.
articles.content: A new adaptation of Pride and Prejudice has been in the works for some time now, and screenwriter Dolly Alderton is sharing her unique perspective on the process through a diary of sorts. To kick off this behind-the-scenes look at making the television event of the year, Alderton met with Dame Emma Thompson over tea. This meeting proved to be an invaluable experience for the screenwriter. The conversation was so enlightening that it overshadowed all other research she had done on Austen in recent months. Thompson's insights were generously shared during their hour-long discussion. She offered thoughtful and well-reasoned answers to Alderton's extensive list of questions. Some of the key takeaways from this meeting include Thompson's assertion that 90 percent of a successful adaptation lies in the casting. A good comedy editor can either make or break a production, according to Thompson. She also emphasized the importance of avoiding over-scoring and letting the dialogue speak for itself. This requires some discipline on the part of the screenwriter, as it is tempting to add more music to heighten the emotional impact of key scenes. In preparation for the project, Alderton has been tasked with creating a document outlining additional dialogue to ensure that the language used stays precise and consistent throughout. She also needs to make sure that the actors are not tempted to improvise in a way that would be anachronistic for the Regency era. The long hours spent pouring over scripts and production notes are finally starting to pay off as the adaptation of Pride and Prejudice nears completion. Despite initial concerns about meeting deadlines, the team is working diligently to incorporate all the necessary cuts and editorial changes. Incorporating director Euros's notes into new drafts by next Friday will be no easy task, but it's a crucial step in ensuring that the final product meets expectations. The pressure to deliver a faithful adaptation of Austen's classic novel weighs heavily on the shoulders of everyone involved. A chance encounter with a fan at a recent event left an indelible impression on one team member. A paralytic woman, drenched in sweat and clutching her cane, cornered them to express her hopes for the upcoming adaptation. Her enthusiasm was palpable, if not a bit daunting. With casting complete, the focus has shifted to rehearsals and costume fittings. The latest addition to the cast is Louis Partridge, who brings a certain je ne sais quoi to the role of Wickham. His presence on set has injected new energy into the production, and his charm has won over even the most skeptical team members. Casting can be a grueling process, with rejections and disappointments weighing heavily on those involved. But when a top choice like Louis Partridge agrees to join the project, it's hard not to feel elated. His enthusiasm for the role is infectious, and his chemistry with the rest of the cast is undeniable. A recent visit to London North Studios provided an opportunity to immerse oneself in the world of Pride and Prejudice. Rows upon rows of exquisite costumes lay on display, each one a testament to the attention to detail that has gone into creating this adaptation. One standout piece caught the eye: Mr. Bennet's embroidered dressing gown. A cast dinner at Lemonia offered a rare chance for team members to let their hair down and socialize outside of the formal setting of the production. Conversations flowed easily, ranging from literature to travel and beyond. The camaraderie was palpable, with even the most seasoned veterans of the industry appearing relaxed and at ease. The evening wore on, with discussions turning to past careers and what might have been if not for a life in acting. Some surprising choices emerged: Louis Partridge would have made a fine documentarian, while Daryl McCormack had a passion for wildlife photography. Emma Corrin's primary school teacher aspirations were met with amusement. As the night drew to a close, team members began to disperse, some heading off to grab a late-night Uber or catch up on work emails. A chance comment from Manda, Netflix executive producer, about Daryl McCormack's mesmerizing eyes provided a lighthearted moment of levity before the evening drew to a close. The production team of Dolly Alderton's lavish new adaptation of Pride and Prejudice had reached a critical juncture in their writing process. On July 22nd, it was time for a read-through of the first three episodes. This marked an important milestone for the writers, as they would finally hear human voices bring their lines to life. The experience was both enlightening and unsettling for the writers. They were able to gauge what sounded natural and what felt forced, but the actors' semi-performances while seated made the dialogue feel somewhat flat. The tension was palpable, making it a challenging day for the writers. As Dolly Alderton took her seat, she began with a heartfelt speech, trying not to get too emotional amidst her excitement and gratitude. Her words were met with warm applause from the cast and crew. It was clear that this production was more than just another adaptation of Austen's classic novel, it was an opportunity for everyone involved to bring something special to the table. The first three episodes received a positive response, exceeding expectations in every way. Fiona Shaw's portrayal of Lady Catherine stood out as particularly impressive, but each and every cast member brought their unique talents to the role. The team felt incredibly fortunate to have such a talented ensemble at their disposal. On July 23rd, the read-through continued with episodes four, five, and six. However, this time around, it was not just the actors who were emotionally invested, the writers themselves found themselves overcome with emotion in the final scenes of episode six. They struggled to maintain their composure, pulling awkward faces as they tried to hold back tears. In a moment of levity, Dolly Alderton couldn't resist texting Jamie Demetriou afterwards to ask what he had taken away from the experience. His response was that the highlight was Jack Lowden's reaction when asked if it was okay to date fellow actors from set. Just over a week later, on July 28th, the team began shooting their first scenes at the Golden Parsonage in Hertfordshire, the chosen location for Longbourn, where they would be based until December. The atmosphere was electric as they embarked on this new chapter in the production process. As the production of Dolly Alderton's lavish new 'Pride and Prejudice' adaptation continues to unfold, the cast and crew are busy bringing the iconic characters to life on screen. The intricate details of the costumes are a testament to the team's dedication to authenticity, with Charlotte, head of costume, selecting fabrics that date back to the 1800s for many of the garments. Among the standout pieces is a playfully embroidered waistcoat designed for Lizzy Bennet, which perfectly captures her lively and adventurous spirit. Meanwhile, icy blues have been chosen to adorn Jane's dresses, complementing Freya Mavor's complexion beautifully. A particular highlight among the costumes is the stunning dress reserved for Lydia, so breathtakingly beautiful that Rhea Norwood has expressed a desire to be buried in it. Charlotte's keen eye for original textiles has undoubtedly paid off, and her choices are sure to delight audiences worldwide. As filming continues, the cast and crew are working tirelessly to perfect their performances, with minor adjustments being made to the script here and there. Lisa has pointed out that a line of Wickham's needs to be revised, due to the recent casting change involving Isabella and her brown eyes. On set, tensions rise as paparazzi manage to snap photos of Emma and Freya during a break on the Longbourn roof. One particularly astute observer notes that Lizzy Bennet would likely not have been seen with a mobile phone in hand, poking fun at the anachronism. As the rain pours down outside, Jack and Dolly take a moment to discuss their characters' motivations, specifically focusing on Darcy's enigmatic nature. The prospect of starting over later without any severance was daunting, especially given her responsibilities as a mother. This led LaSane to reconsider her initial dismissal of the exit offer. Her business had initially focused on helping young people find meaningful career paths, but after leaving Google, its scope expanded to include workshops for women and an app offering her expertise at scale. articles.title: Dark Matter Comprises Multiple Particles with Varying Properties
articles.summary: Researchers have discovered evidence that suggests dark matter is made up of several particles, which could interact and combine to form complex entities.
articles.content: Scientists have long debated whether dark matter comprises a single type of particle or multiple particles with varying properties. The possibility that dark matter is made up of several particles has gained momentum after researchers discovered convincing evidence of a dark matter particle earlier this year. This discovery opens up the intriguing prospect that these particles could interact and combine with one another to form complex entities, much like ordinary atoms and molecules. Researchers are now pondering whether these "dark particles could follow their own set of rules, forming different classes of nuclei and atoms. The idea is not entirely new, as scientists have previously tackled similar challenges in understanding the diversity of ordinary matter. The researchers' hypothesis proposes a mirror sector within our universe where particles that barely interact with visible matter would have their own forces and be able to interact with one another. This idea may sound like science fiction, but it's rooted in a theory proposed two decades ago as a solution to the problem of the Higgs boson's mass. The Mirror Twin Higgs concept was designed to offset certain quantum effects that might cause its mass to be much greater than observed. Physicist Zackaria Chacko, one of the creators of this theory, is now part of an investigation extending this hypothesis into the realm of dark matter. Along with collaborators, he explores what would happen if particles from the hypothetical mirror sector could combine, forming nuclei, atoms, and various dark elements. The team's calculations suggest that under certain conditions, these particles could merge to create dark equivalents of familiar elements, ranging from simple forms to more complex ones like carbon. This raises intriguing questions about the composition and behavior of dark matter in our universe. This concept may seem far-fetched, but it offers a potential explanation for the organization of dark matter, which has long been a puzzle for scientists seeking to understand its diversity. The concept of a dark periodic table aims to categorize the diverse properties of invisible particles thought to make up dark matter. Different masses and properties among these particles would alter the rules governing their interactions, influencing the structures they can form and their stability. This would be a significant departure from the behavior of ordinary matter's elements. The researchers' model suggests that dark hydrogen atoms, akin to our universe's most basic element, are inherently unstable and unlikely to persist as intact entities. This contrasts starkly with hydrogen's ubiquity in normal matter, where it's considered an essential building block. The instability of these hypothetical particles is a crucial aspect of understanding their behavior. A dark periodic table" would provide a framework for classifying the unique properties of dark elements, much like its counterpart helped organize the known elements in our universe. This classification system would be indispensable if scientists were to discover and study these enigmatic particles. However, the existence of such structures remains purely theoretical. While it's uncertain whether dark matter's invisible atoms could actually form, researchers acknowledge that there is still much to uncover about this phenomenon. Theoretical physics currently provides the foundation for understanding dark matter's properties and behavior, but direct observation or experimental evidence would be necessary to confirm these theories. articles.title: Microsoft, JPMorgan Chase, Atalanta
articles.summary: Flights were grounded, banking operations froze, and email went dark in recent cyber crises, prompting officials to ask who was behind these disruptions. However, investigations revealed...
articles.content: Flights were grounded, banking operations froze, and email went dark in recent cyber crises, prompting officials to ask who was behind these disruptions. However, investigations revealed that a software defect at Microsoft and an internal bug at JPMorgan Chase were the culprits. These issues had gone unnoticed for months, leading to unforeseen system behavior. As senior officials at the White House's Office of the National Cyber Director, we witnessed this pattern repeatedly: organizations responsible for critical systems struggled to anticipate how their systems would behave in normal, abnormal, or hostile conditions. This lack of confidence was a recurring theme during our tenure at the White House. The first indication that commercial space had become a front line of conflict came with Russia's invasion of Ukraine. A cyberattack knocked out tens of thousands of modems operated by an American satellite company, disrupting remote monitoring for thousands of German wind turbines and causing widespread connectivity losses across Europe. These events highlighted the need for Washington to gain a clearer understanding of the industry's exposure. The scale and complexity of these disruptions underscored the importance of verifying critical systems' behavior under various conditions, a challenge that Atalanta, our current company focused on mathematical AI solutions, aims to address. As we delved into the world of industry operators, one thing became painfully clear: legacy satellites are operating far beyond their intended lifespan, and prime contractors have limited visibility into the risks posed by subcontractors. This lack of oversight creates a ticking time bomb, with potential consequences that can be catastrophic. The Volt Typhoon incident served as a stark reminder of this vulnerability. Chinese state hackers infiltrated civilian infrastructure, remaining undetected in some networks for years, poised to disrupt essential services in a future conflict. The fact that national security is intertwined with even the most mundane aspects of daily life, such as water utilities and ports, is a sobering reality. Our experiences at the White House informed the development of Back to the Building Blocks , a report that highlighted the limitations of eliminating known software vulnerabilities. Even if every flaw were eradicated, unknown weaknesses and unforeseen interactions would still leave critical systems vulnerable to attack. The report proposed three technical approaches: memory safe programming languages; secure chip architectures; and formal methods. Five months after its release, a faulty CrowdStrike update brought flights to a standstill and disrupted hospitals. One of the world's most advanced cybersecurity companies failed to anticipate the consequences of its own software update, causing damage on par with what a hostile nation might aim to achieve. Experts pointed to the Building Blocks report as a solution to the unfolding crisis. The scale and complexity of these disruptions underscored the importance of verifying critical systems' behavior under various conditions, a challenge that remains a pressing concern in the industry today. The recent spate of tech outages has eerie echoes of 2024's disruptions, where widespread chaos ensued without any evidence of a coordinated cyberattack. This phenomenon is known as the Software Understanding gap, and its economic toll is staggering - at least $2.41 trillion annually in the US alone. Artificial intelligence is exacerbating the problem by churning out software at breakneck speed, introducing autonomous systems whose behavior is increasingly difficult to predict. The consequences of this widening gap are far-reaching, with critical infrastructure vulnerable to disruptions that can have devastating effects on businesses and communities. Closing the Software Understanding gap requires a concerted effort to bring high-assurance engineering to critical sectors. Testing can only reveal how a system behaves under limited conditions, but formal methods can provide assurance that critical requirements hold across a broad range of scenarios. DARPA's HACMS program is an exemplary initiative in this area - it used formal methods to bolster the security of an unmanned helicopter, which expert hackers failed to breach. This level of assurance must be maintained as systems evolve and become more complex. The US government has started to take steps to address the issue. The Senate Armed Services Committee has instructed the Pentagon to develop a strategy for integrating formal methods research into production environments. Meanwhile, the Department of Energy has identified Software Understanding as a core priority under its Genesis Mission initiative. Government agencies funding new critical infrastructure systems should prioritize a deep understanding of software behavior to prevent future cyber crises. This means ensuring that regulators across 16 key sectors make rigorous software assurance a standard expectation in their operations. While it's impossible to predict the cause of the next failure, whether it's a state-sponsored attack, an unpredictable AI agent, or a routine software update gone wrong, one thing is clear: we need a far better grasp of our own systems before disaster strikes. articles.title: Household Cleaning Product Mixtures Pose Health Risks
articles.summary: Combining certain household cleaning products can lead to health problems due to the release of toxic gases.
articles.content: A common practice in household cleaning can be hazardous to one's health when not done properly. Some tough stains require extra effort and elbow grease to remove completely. To tackle these stubborn messes, some people might consider combining multiple cleaning products, hoping for a more effective solution. However, this approach raises concerns about the potential dangers of mixing different chemicals. Experts have debunked a long-standing myth that combining household cleaners can produce mustard gas, a toxic chemical used in World War I battles. While it is not possible to create mustard gas from typical household cleaning products, combining certain chemicals can lead to health problems. Chemical reactions between some cleaning products can release gases that irritate the body's sensitive areas. When bleach and ammonia-based cleaners are mixed, they produce chloramines, a compound that poses serious health risks when inhaled. When bleach reacts with certain chemicals, it can release chlorine atoms that replace hydrogen atoms in other compounds to form chloramines. These toxic substances are particularly hazardous when inhaled in high concentrations. Delphine Farmer, an atmospheric chemist at Colorado State University, has studied the effects of chloramines on human health. Chloramines are common contaminants found indoors and outdoors, often as a result of using bleach for cleaning or swimming in pools that have been treated with chlorine-based chemicals. We frequently encounter them in various environments, Farmer stated. The presence of these toxic compounds can be attributed to the widespread use of bleach and other disinfectants. Mixing bleach with acidic substances can also produce hazardous gases, including chlorine gas, which irritates the eyes and skin. This noxious fume has a distinctive odor reminiscent of swimming pools. Furthermore, combining certain cleaning products can lead to the formation of other toxic compounds, such as chloramines. However, mustard gas is not typically produced through these chemical reactions. The severity of exposure to these hazardous substances depends on various factors, including concentration and duration of exposure. Chary noted that while some cleaning products may contain sulfur, which is a key component of mustard gas, the conditions required for its formation are usually met at elevated temperatures and pressures. The severity of exposure to hazardous byproducts from mixing cleaning products can be mitigated by factors such as room size and ventilation. In a larger room with adequate airflow, the concentration of potentially toxic substances is likely to be lower than in a smaller, poorly ventilated space. Individuals with pre-existing health conditions like asthma or lung disease may experience more severe reactions to exposure due to their compromised respiratory systems. This exacerbation can lead to further complications and worsening symptoms. Household cleaning products generally contain low concentrations of the chemicals involved in potential reactions, thereby reducing the risk of significant harm if an accidental mixture occurs. Household bleach, for instance, is formulated at a concentration that limits its potency compared to industrial-strength versions. If someone inadvertently mixes cleaning agents and notices immediate adverse effects, such as coughing or eye irritation, it is crucial to quickly move outside to fresh air. This can help alleviate symptoms and prevent further exposure to the hazardous byproducts. Medical treatment for chloramine exposure typically involves administering medications such as albuterol to widen air passages and monitoring oxygen saturation levels in patients' lungs for signs of damage. To minimize risks associated with mixing cleaning products, experts recommend storing oxidizing cleaners like bleach and hydrogen peroxide separately from other household chemicals. When tackling tough stains, it's best to wait until the initial cleaner has lost its potency before applying a second product, as this reduces the likelihood of creating hazardous byproducts. articles.title: Amazon Tops Fortune 500 List for First Time
articles.summary: Amazon has surpassed Walmart as the world's largest entity by revenue, according to the 2026 Fortune Global 500 list.
articles.content: Amazon's dominance in the global market has reached new heights as it topped the 2026 Fortune 500 list for the first time, ending Walmart's 13-year reign at the top spot. The company's vast reach encompasses a wide range of industries, from streaming services and cloud computing to grocery stores and home security cameras. Its expansion has been marked by significant acquisitions, including MGM and Twitch, in addition to its core business of shipping goods worldwide. Jeff Bezos' prediction that Amazon would one day go bankrupt is a stark contrast to the company's current status as the world's largest entity by revenue, according to the 2026 Fortune Global 500 list. This achievement was announced just a month after it took the top spot on the Fortune 500 list in June. In a candid assessment made at an all-hands meeting in November 2018, Bezos expressed his belief that large companies often have limited lifespans, stating "Amazon is not too big to fail. In fact, I predict one day Amazon will fail. Amazon will go bankrupt." Amazon's remarkable journey has led it to join an elite group in the Fortune 500 rankings. With four companies having held the top spot since its inception in 1955, Amazon is now among them, alongside General Motors, Exxon Mobil, and Walmart. One of these companies has already fulfilled Bezos' prophecy of going bankrupt. General Motors, which initially occupied the No. 1 position for decades, filed for bankruptcy in June 2009. This move marked a significant turning point for GM, as it sought to restructure and regain its footing. GM's bankruptcy process was lengthy and complex. By the end of 2009, the company had undergone significant changes, including the departure of four brands: Pontiac, Saturn, Hummer, and Saab. The once-iconic American automaker also found itself in a precarious financial situation, with American taxpayers emerging as its largest shareholders. Despite this setback, GM was able to revive itself and remains a prominent player in the Fortune 500 rankings. This outcome serves as a testament to the company's resilience and ability to adapt to changing circumstances. The warning issued by Jeff Bezos remains unchanged over the past eight years. His message is a stern reminder that Amazon's very existence depends on its ability to innovate and prioritize customer satisfaction above all else. For those who have worked under his leadership, it's clear that he takes this prediction seriously. They attest that Amazon will eventually cease to exist. Research conducted by scientists at the Santa Fe Institute in 2015 shed new light on what drives a company's demise. Tracking over 25,000 publicly traded North American companies from 1950 to 2009, they found no correlation between a company's lifespan and its product offerings or longevity. The study revealed that the average public company lasts around a decade before being acquired, merged, or liquidated. This outcome serves as a testament to the company's resilience and ability to adapt to changing circumstances. The researchers' findings challenge Bezos' 30-year rule by suggesting that it's not about how long a company has been in business. Marcus Hamilton, corresponding author of the study, made it clear that companies across various industries face similar risks. When asked about his research, he noted, “It doesn't matter if you're selling bananas, airplanes, or whatever,” highlighting the universality of this trend. The spending spree at Amazon shows no signs of slowing down as it pours billions into capital projects. The company's plans to invest around $220 billion this year alone are a testament to its ambition and growth strategy under new CEO Andy Jassy. As the company continues to expand its cloud computing business, Amazon Web Services (AWS), and explore the possibilities of generative AI, its spending is expected to reach unprecedented levels. According to Jassy's comments on the company's third-quarter earnings call, only one Fortune 500 company has ever reached $1 trillion in annual revenue, but he believes that AWS and Amazon's retail business could join this exclusive club within five to ten years. articles.title: Epigenome Editing Shows Promise in Human Trials
articles.summary: A groundbreaking new approach to gene editing is emerging, one that doesn't alter genes but rather controls their expression. This technique, known as epigenome editing, has already shown...
articles.content: A groundbreaking new approach to gene editing is emerging, one that doesn't alter genes but rather controls their expression. This technique, known as epigenome editing, has already shown promise in human trials and could revolutionize the treatment of a wide range of conditions. Researchers are hailing the first human trials of epigenome editing as a major breakthrough, with early results demonstrating its effectiveness. According to Charles Gersbach, a leading expert in the field, this new approach holds tremendous potential for treating diseases that have long been poorly understood. The ability to turn genes on or off rather than altering them is a significant departure from traditional gene editing techniques like CRISPR. This means that epigenome editing can be used to treat conditions where a specific gene is overactive or underactive, without making permanent changes to the genome. Epigenome editing could also have a profound impact on our understanding of human biology and disease, said Gersbach. By allowing biologists to explore how genes are expressed in different contexts, this new approach could lead to major breakthroughs in the treatment of common conditions that currently puzzle scientists. Hepatitis B remains a puzzling condition for scientists due to its unique ability to evade the immune system by hiding within liver cells in circular loops of viral DNA. This hidden form of the virus also integrates into the genome of liver cells, increasing the risk of cancer and making it difficult to treat effectively with current medications. According to Gersbach, each infected cell can harbor dozens of copies of this viral genome, further complicating efforts to eradicate the disease. The standard CRISPR gene editing approach is not a viable solution due to its high risk of causing chromosomal abnormalities or even cancer by introducing multiple DNA cuts at once. This problem arises from the potential for incorrect ends being joined together during the repair process, highlighting the need for alternative methods. To control genes instead of editing them, researchers are modifying the standard CRISPR gene editing tool to use an enzyme that adds methyl tags rather than cutting DNA. This approach essentially converts a gene editor into an epigenome editor, allowing scientists to make targeted changes to gene expression without altering the underlying DNA sequence. Early attempts at creating these modified editors showed promise, but their effects were short-lived, lasting only a few days according to Angelo Lombardo of San Raffaele University in Italy. Lombardo's team overcame this limitation by linking parts of three different enzymes to a de-scissored CRISPR Cas9 protein, which successfully made the desired epigenetic changes. Animal studies have demonstrated that these modified editors can permanently shut down gene activity, with the effect being passed on when cells divide, much like natural methylation. Researchers are excited about a new approach to gene control using epigenetic editing, which has shown promise in animal studies. Epigenetic editing is a type of gene regulation that doesn't involve cutting DNA like traditional CRISPR Cas9 gene editing does, according to Marianne Rots at the University Medical Center Groningen. This method has been found to be reversible and maintained over time. The potential benefits of epigenetic editing are vast, as it can control gene activity without the risks associated with DNA cuts. While it may not be able to correct disease-causing mutations like more advanced forms of CRISPR, controlling gene expression alone could lead to significant breakthroughs in treating inherited conditions. Recent studies have shown that epigenetic editing can achieve similar results to traditional CRISPR treatments, such as the first approved treatment for sickle cell disease. This therapy works by disabling the "off switch for fetal hemoglobin production, and researchers believe that epigenome editors could also accomplish this goal. The use of epigenome editors has raised concerns about their potential drawbacks, despite being considered safer than traditional CRISPR gene editing methods. One major issue is that these editors can be unpredictable in how they affect cells, as the complexities of gene regulation mean one editor may work well for some genes but not others. This variability could lead to unintended consequences and make it difficult to achieve consistent results. The challenge of predicting which epigenome editors will work effectively in specific circumstances has been a focus of research. Stylianos Tsagkris, a researcher at the European Molecular Biology Laboratory in Rome, is working on developing a method to assess how well different editors perform by targeting thousands of sites simultaneously. Researchers are also exploring ways to improve existing epigenetic editors, which can be cumbersome and even harmful to cells due to their large size. For instance, some CRISPR-based editors consist of a modified Cas9 enzyme fused with other enzymes, making them difficult to deliver effectively. To address these limitations, researchers have turned to advanced computational tools like AlphaFold, an artificial intelligence system that can design more efficient epigenome editors by binding existing enzymes in cells rather than relying on cumbersome fusion proteins. Researchers have been exploring new ways to harness the power of epigenome editing, a process that involves controlling gene expression rather than making permanent changes to DNA sequences. This approach is inspired by the complex interactions between proteins in natural systems, where multiple molecules bind together to perform specific functions. Designing new proteins that can target specific locations within cells has become increasingly sophisticated, thanks to advances in computational tools like AlphaFold. However, delivering these epigenome editors to the desired organs remains a significant challenge, with the liver currently being one of the few accessible targets. The ability to target other organs, particularly the brain, would have far-reaching implications for treating a wide range of diseases. The potential benefits of targeting the brain are vast, as it is often the site of mental illnesses and neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's and multiple sclerosis. According to Jamie Hackett at EMBL, Ninety per cent of the interesting targets are in the brain, so when we can target that, the field will really take off."
